one_liner: JSON-document CRDT, Rust core compiled to WebAssembly; much faster and smaller than pure-JS Automerge 0.14, slower than Yjs and Loro.
what_it_does: Automerge keeps a JSON-like document (nested maps, lists, text with rich-text marks, counters, timestamps) that several replicas edit offline and merge deterministically, with full change history, heads/forkAt time travel, a compact binary file format and a sync protocol. The JavaScript package @automerge/automerge (3.5.0) wraps @automerge/automerge-wasm, built from the Rust crate automerge (0.12.0); a C library (automerge-c) shares the same core. The JS API is functional: Automerge.change(doc, d => ...) returns a new document, save()/load() and saveIncremental()/loadIncremental() move bytes, and merge() combines replicas. Relative to the 0.14 pure-JS baseline it is the same project and data model but not a drop-in: text editing goes through splice() on strings in the current API and the storage format changed.
how_it_is_fast: The pure-JS 0.14 line kept every operation as JS objects and saved history as JSON, which is why its B4 document was 84 MB and its heap 1.1 GB. The Rust core stores operations in the columnar, run-length and delta encoded format of the Automerge binary spec (hexane crate: Column, PrefixColumn and DeltaColumn types that support splice directly on compressed bytes in O(log n + affected bytes)), and since Automerge 3 the in-memory op set (op_set2) uses that columnar form too, which the project credits with a 10x-plus memory cut (blog, snippet only). List and text positions are resolved through hexane's PrefixColumn, which keeps per-slab running sums in a B-tree for O(log n) offset queries; compression uses flate2 with the pure-Rust zlib-rs backend, and the release profile builds with LTO and one codegen unit.
when_to_use: Local-first JavaScript or TypeScript apps that need a general JSON document model (maps, lists, text, counters) with merge, history and a ready-made sync protocol, rather than only a text CRDT.

Projects still on Automerge 0.14 or 1.0-era JS: the old implementation is the baseline that collapses on long histories (crdt-benchmarks B4: 489,104 ms and an 83,966,886-byte document; automerge-perf: old Automerge.Text ran out of memory after about 235,000 operations at Node's ~1.4 GB default heap).

Storage- or bandwidth-sensitive persistence of whole documents: in the 2024 suite run its saved documents were the smallest of the four libraries (B4 129,116 bytes vs Yjs 159,929 and Loro 258,228; B1.1 3,992 vs 6,031).
Polyglot stacks that want one binary format across Rust servers, C/FFI clients and browser or Node front ends (Node, browsers via a bundler or the base64 entry point, Deno, Cloudflare workerd).
when_not_to_use: Keystroke-rate text editing where per-op latency matters most: in the same run Automerge 2.1.10 trailed Yjs (pure JS) and Loro (wasm) on every quoted text row (B1.1 365 vs 188 and 120 ms; B1.3 307 vs 119 and 81 ms; B4 14,326 vs 5,714 and 3,089 ms).
Many clients writing concurrently to one map or array: B3.1-B3.4 took 1,632-2,780 ms against 56-299 ms for Yjs, ywasm and Loro, with larger update messages (B3.1 283,296 bytes vs 49,169 for Yjs).

Fast cold load of large documents on the main thread: B4 parseTime 1,805 ms vs 13-39 ms for the others; open issue #1244 reports a large doc blocking the main thread for 10+ seconds, and a community run in #1201 (Automerge 3.2.1 wasm) loads a 200,000-update snapshot in 535 ms vs 24 ms for Yjs.
Bundle-size-sensitive pages: the measured wasm is 1,737,571 bytes (604,118 gzipped) vs Yjs's 69,124 (20,100), and the 3.5.0 npm package unpacks to about 47.5 MB across its many entry points.

Native Rust write-heavy services on recent crates without benchmarking first: open issue #1387 shows map-insert throughput falling from 158,621 to 9,742 files/s between crate 0.6.1 and 0.11.0 (maintainer re-run), and #1591 shows applying one remote keystroke growing linearly with text length since 0.7 (13.38 ms vs 0.006 ms at 124,018 characters).

integration.form: npm module (@automerge/automerge over @automerge/automerge-wasm), crate (automerge), C library (automerge-c)
integration.dependencies: JS: none beyond the bundled wasm; browsers need a bundler with async WebAssembly (webpack asyncWebAssembly) or the base64 entry point. Rust: hexane, flate2 (zlib-rs), sha2, leb128, rustc-hash, smol_str, tinyvec, unicode-segmentation, rand, tracing and others
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.90 (rust-version in Cargo.toml); the wasm build also needs nightly with rust-src (std rebuilt with panic=unwind so panics surface as JS exceptions), wasm-bindgen-cli and wasm-opt; automerge-c needs cmake, cmocka, doxygen and ninja
integration.platforms: any Rust target; wasm32 for Node, browsers, Deno and workerd (32-bit wasm memory cap; Memory64 support is open issue #1107)
integration.thread_safety: not documented for the wasm build; JS documents are immutable snapshots updated by change(), and wasm-side allocations are freed by FinalizationRegistry or must be freed explicitly on platforms without it
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: same project, data model and change/merge style as Automerge 0.14, but the binary format, text API and package layout changed, so code and stored documents need migration

gotchas: Harness note: the only speed evidence is cross-run. The 2.1.10 column (i5-8400, Node 20.5.0, Jan 2024) and the 0.14.1 column (older table, machine and Node not stated) come from different runs; Yjs itself moved from 303 to 188 ms on B1.1 between them, so ratios such as 272x on B1.3 mix version and machine effects. Only machine-independent columns compare cleanly: B4 docSize 83,966,886 vs 129,116 bytes (about 650x smaller, derived from page data) and B1.1 docSize 2,161,851 vs 3,992 bytes.

Harness note: the suite's memUsed is process.memoryUsage().heapUsed after a forced GC, clamped at zero, so wasm linear memory is invisible and Automerge's '0 B' rows say nothing. The README's B4 section says all actions are replayed in a single transaction because Automerge ran out of memory, but js-lib/b4.js calls insertText/deleteText per edit, each wrapped in automerge.change plus saveIncremental, and the results note says the opposite; and the table (ywasm 0.9.3) predates the suite's last harness commits of Feb 12, 2024 ('ensure that the benchmarks also extract content', ywasm bumped to 0.17), so it was not regenerated against the HEAD code.

The measured 2.1.10 is not what you install today: the Automerge team wrote the suite's adapter (alexjg PR #22, the 'next' API; B3.3 stores RawString instead of text CRDTs to avoid memory blow-up), Automerge 3 rewrote the in-memory representation, and the Rust core has open write-path regressions (#1387, #1591), so 2024 timings do not predict 3.5.0 in either direction.

saveIncremental() chunks are less compressed than a full save() (automerge-wasm README), so append-only logs should be compacted with periodic save(); historical queries at old heads are not indexed and are slower unless you forkAt().
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Loro is faster on every text and map row of the same 2024 run and also ships as wasm, diamond-types merges text traces faster in the Eg-walker paper, and Yjs or ywasm have far smaller bundles; pick Automerge when you need its full JSON document model with history, sync protocol and C/Rust/JS bindings on one documented binary format, and when the smallest saved documents matter more than per-keystroke speed.
verified_claims_summary: dmonad/crdt-benchmarks (N=6000, Node) shows Automerge 2.1.10, the Rust core compiled to wasm, at 365 ms (B1.1 append), 307 ms (B1.3 prepend) and 14,326 ms (B4 real editing trace) on an i5-8400 with Node 20.5.0, against 2,460, 83,488 and 489,104 ms for pure-JS Automerge 0.14.1 in an older table with no machine or Node version stated, so the 6.7x to 272x speedups are cross-run (tier D). In the same run Automerge 2.1.10 is slower than Yjs 13.6.11 and Loro 0.10.1 on all three rows; the robust cross-version gain is document size (B4 84 MB to 129 KB).
status_note: Actively maintained by Ink & Switch staff (MIT, 6.7k stars, last commit 2026-10-09, @automerge/automerge 3.5.0 and crate 0.12.0 released 2026-09-16, about 694k crate downloads), production-usable from JS; the README calls the Rust API low level and not well documented, and the only public cross-library numbers date from January 2024 (issue #1201 asks for new ones).
